title: probabilistic onboard sampler and batched release summaries
author: Leah Park
description:
Context: Onboard inflow for low-throughput or bursty models was producing noisy release notes and uneven sampling coverage for lifecycle metrics. This PR introduces a probabilistic, workload-aware onboard sampler plus a batched release digest compiler to make changelogs more concise and statistically representative.

Motivation: Reduce manual curation on small-model onboarding, improve signal quality for perf and cost profiles, and produce deterministic-but-compressed release digests for downstream ingestion by release pipelines.

Summary of changes: - Add probabilistic_sampler.py: reservoir + stratified bucketing that weights samples by recent request trace counts, model size, and declared sensitivity tags. Default sampler is a hybrid: for high-traffic models it falls back to deterministic head-sampling; for low/no-traffic it runs an epsilon-greedy reservoir with decayed weights. - Add batched_release_compiler.py: composes multiple small onboarding changes into a single digest with summarized metrics (latency histogram, token cost delta, affinity hints) and canonical provenance fingerprints. - Introduce synthetic_probe_runner.py: optional probe harness that seeds low-traffic models with synthetic lightweight workloads to collect baseline perf if real traffic is insufficient. Probe runner respects privacy flags and bypasses telem export when marked. - Add contract_validator augment that enforces sampler-config presence and annotates manifests with sampling seed + policy. - CI/workflow updated to run sampler integration test and ensure release digests are generated in a dry-run mode during merges to main. - Documentation and release note templates for reviewer consumption.

Design notes (brief): - Sampling algorithm: stratified reservoir with 3 strata (high, medium, low traffic) computed from seven-day rolling counts. Each stratum maintains an adaptive reservoir size proportional to expected entropy; an importance weight decays exponentially (alpha=0.97) for older traces. Edge cases: models with strict PII flags will be excluded from synthetic probing and only allow on-device sampling if configured. - Release batching heuristics: releases occurring within a 72-hour window are candidates for consolidation if their delta footprint (additions+deletions token-change metric) is below a configurable threshold (default 500 tokens). The compiler generates a short digest plus an expanded JSON artifact where needed for audit. - Backwards compatibility: sampler-config.yaml supports legacy manifest linting; the sampler will default to legacy behaviour for manifests lacking the new sampling contract.

Checklist: - [x] Implement sampler and compile unit tests - [x] Integrate sampler into onboard pipeline (dry-run) - [x] Add probe harness and privacy gating - [x] Add docs and release templates - [x] Add CI workflow to generate release digests on PR merges

Commits (high-level): - add probabilistic sampler and docs - implement batched release compiler and template - add synthetic probe harness with privacy gate - augment contract validator to require sampler config - add unit and integration tests + CI workflow - fix edge cases and handle legacy manifests - update helm values and release note changelog

Test summary: - Unit tests: sampler edge cases, reservoir correctness, weight decay. - Integration: onboard pipeline dry-run generates digest.json matching template; CI verifies digest field presence. - Manual validation: author ran probe against a staging model: baseline latency, memory, and token-cost deltas collected and embedded in a sample digest.

Review conversation (high level): - Anu Shah: "Nice approach. Two asks: (1) please document failure modes if probe fails (network/timeout), and (2) make sampler-config defaults explicit in README." Response: "Added explicit failure semantics and default table in README; probe now uses exponential backoff and marks model as 'probe-failed' in audit log." - Diego Martínez: "Can we make the digest include an optional 'rollback-suggest' flag when perf regresses > 25%?" Response: "Added heuristic: digest includes rollback_suggest when 95th latency increases > 25% and token-cost delta > 10%." - Ravi Patel: "Concern about CI runtime cost given probe: ensure probes run only in staging and are off by default." Response: "Probes run in CI only as dry-run stub that validates templates; full probes are gated by 'enable_probes' config and off by default in CI."

Approvals: - Anu Shah approved (2025-09-08) - Diego Martínez approved (2025-09-09) - Ravi Patel approved (2025-09-10)

merge_outcome: Merged to main via squash by release-bot on 2025-09-10 after all reviewers approved and CI passed. Generated release digest artifact committed to changelogs/ and a dry-run digest emitted by CI for audit. No rollback was triggered during merge.
release_notes: Adds workload-aware probabilistic sampling for onboarding and a batched release digest compiler. Improves representativeness of onboarding telemetry for low-traffic models, and reduces churn in release notes by consolidating small changes into a concise digest. Optional synthetic probe harness can seed baselines for low-traffic models (disabled by default).
notes_for_ops: When deploying to Private clusters, set enable_probes=false in registry values to avoid synthetic traffic. The sampler config uses a default alpha=0.97 decay; tune via onboard/configs/sampler-config.yaml. Ensure CI secrets for probe runners are not present in production or private air-gapped deployments.
